issues.title: deep_copy calls nova_rt_struct_alloc(nslots*8) -- loses the type-id of the original
issues.detail: At nova_runtime.c line 2297, `deep_copy` creates the destination struct via `nova_rt_struct_alloc(nslots * 8)`. With the new 2-arg signature `nova_rt_struct_alloc(int64_t size, int64_t type_id)`, this call would need the source struct's type-id. But deep_copy does NOT know the type-id of the source -- it only has the raw pointer. The design proposes changing the signature to require a type_id argument but never addresses this call site. If deep_copy passes 0 (or the C compiler rejects a 1-arg call to a 2-arg function), every deep-copied struct -- including every struct sent through a channel (channels deep-copy on send) and every copy() call -- loses its type-id. The deep-copied struct would then have type-id 0 = 'unregistered', so json_stringify and str() on a struct received from a channel would render as a raw integer instead of a JSON object. This is exactly the 'partial coverage creates silent corruption' failure mode (iter-31-34 mode 4) the design claims to avoid. Fix: deep_copy must read NOVA_STRUCT_TYPEID(src) from the source and pass it to the allocation call.
issues.fix: In deep_copy's struct branch, extract the type-id from the source via NOVA_STRUCT_TYPEID(p) and pass it as the second argument to nova_rt_struct_alloc. Same for nova_result_pack (line 11473) which also calls nova_rt_struct_alloc with 1 arg.

issues.title: nova_result_pack calls nova_rt_struct_alloc with 1 arg -- compile error or silent corruption
issues.detail: At nova_runtime.c line 11473, `nova_result_pack` calls `nova_rt_struct_alloc((int64_t)sizeof(NovaResult))` -- a hardcoded C-level call with 1 argument. The design changes the signature to 2 arguments `(int64_t size, int64_t type_id)` but does not mention this call site. Since C does not have default arguments, this will be a compile error (if the compiler is strict) or UB (if a stale declaration is used). Result values are the foundation of NOVA's error handling; if this breaks, every ok()/err() call crashes. The design's Section 3 ('Compiler Changes') lists all LLVM-emitted call sites but ignores C-code call sites in the runtime itself.
issues.fix: Update nova_result_pack to pass type_id=0 (Results are not user-defined structs and should not carry metadata). Also audit aligned_struct_alloc's pass-through at line 508.

issues.title: aligned_struct_alloc delegates to nova_rt_struct_alloc but has wrong arity after signature change
issues.detail: At nova_runtime.c line 508, `nova_rt_aligned_struct_alloc(size, alignment)` calls `return nova_rt_struct_alloc(size)` for alignment <= 16. After the signature change to `nova_rt_struct_alloc(int64_t size, int64_t type_id)`, this becomes a 1-arg call to a 2-arg function -- compile error. The design Section 3B mentions changing `aligned_struct_alloc` in the LLVM declaration (line 16270) but NOT the internal C delegation at line 508. Furthermore, the design does not change aligned_struct_alloc's own signature to accept a type_id, nor does it change the LLVM-emitted call at compiler line 15085 to pass a type_id. The aligned path (for @repr(align(N)) structs with N>16) would silently get type_id=0 from the alignment argument being misinterpreted, or fail to compile.
issues.fix: Change aligned_struct_alloc's signature to (int64_t size, int64_t alignment, int64_t type_id), update the delegation to pass type_id through, update the high-alignment codepath at line 523 to pack type_id, and update the LLVM-emitted call at compiler line 15085 to pass the type_id.

issues.title: gen3 (bootstrap) codegen emits 1-arg nova_rt_struct_alloc -- link failure breaks bootstrap
issues.detail: The bootstrap codegen path at nova_compiler.nova line 3987 (`codegen_call`) emits `call ptr @nova_rt_struct_alloc(i64 ...)` with a 1-arg call, and the declaration at line 5847 is `declare ptr @nova_rt_struct_alloc(i64) nounwind`. After the runtime changes the C function to 2 args, the gen3-compiled LLVM IR has a signature mismatch: the call passes 1 arg but the linker sees a 2-arg symbol. On most ABIs this produces UB (the second arg is whatever garbage was in the register). If the garbage type_id happens to be > 255 it saturates to 0 (benign), but if it is in [1,255] it writes a bogus type-id into the tag word, corrupting the nslots field (since the design repurposes bits 8-15). This makes NOVA_STRUCT_NSLOTS return wrong values for EVERY struct allocated by gen3-compiled code, causing deep_copy to walk the wrong number of slots -> silent memory corruption or crash. The bootstrap chain (gen3 compiles gen4, gen4 compiles gen5) means gen3 must also emit the new signature.
issues.fix: The gen3 codegen at line 3987 and declaration at line 5847 must be updated to pass a type_id argument (likely 0 for gen3, which has no struct type registry). This MUST be done in the same commit or the bootstrap chain breaks.

issues.title: Closures allocated via make_closure get a type_id argument but are not in ire_struct_type_ids -- what value?
issues.detail: Closures are allocated at compiler line 15286 via nova_rt_struct_alloc. The design's Section 3B changes make_struct codegen to pass type_id, but the make_closure codegen at line 15283-15286 is NOT mentioned. If the design updates nova_rt_struct_alloc to require 2 args, the closure allocation must also pass a type_id (presumably 0). The design mentions closures only in the comment 'Slot 0 is the type hash (non-repr-C struct) or fn ptr (closure)' but never addresses the codegen site. If the closure codegen is not updated, the compiler emits a 1-arg call to a 2-arg function -- LLVM IR type mismatch, which is either rejected by the verifier or produces UB. More subtly: if a type_id is accidentally set on a closure, nova_struct_meta_for's cross-check (slot-0 hash vs registered hash) would compare a function pointer against a type hash and could coincidentally pass (1/2^64 chance per closure, but at scale this is nonzero), causing the runtime to try to render the closure as a struct with named fields, reading captures as if they were struct fields -- silent garbage output.
issues.fix: Explicitly pass type_id=0 for all make_closure allocations. Document that type_id=0 means 'no metadata' and is the escape valve for non-struct STRUCT-tagged objects.

issues.title: nslots reduction from 13-bit to 5-bit breaks eq/hash for structs with 32+ fields (SILENT correctness bug admitted and deferred)
issues.detail: The design explicitly acknowledges in Section 4C that for structs with nslots saturated at 31, eq and hash only compare/hash 31 fields instead of all N fields. This means two structs differing only in field 32+ would compare as equal (== returns true when it should return false) and hash identically (collisions). The design defers this to 'Stage S5' and adds a compile-time guard at S0 to reject >30-field structs. However: (a) the compile-time guard is at the STRUCT DEFINITION site, not at every NSLOTS consumer, so if the guard is accidentally removed or bypassed the bug silently reappears; (b) the compiler's own IrBuilder struct (mentioned in the design as having ~30 fields) is AT the boundary -- if it ever gains 1 more field, eq/hash/deep_copy/rc_free silently under-walk. The design says 'no real NOVA program hits it' but the compiler ITSELF is very close. Furthermore, the 31-slot hard cap affects closures too: a closure capturing 31+ variables (rare but legal, e.g. in deeply nested generated code) would have its captures silently truncated on deep_copy/free, causing memory leaks or use-after-free.
issues.fix: The compile-time guard is necessary but not sufficient. The nslots==31 metadata fallback must ship in S1 (not deferred to S5) for rc_free and deep_copy at minimum, since those are correctness-critical. eq/hash can be deferred.

issues.title: Reconverge non-determinism: existing struct registration iterates keys(e.ire_struct_types) in insertion order, but insertion order depends on codegen visitation order
issues.detail: The design proposes sorting ire_struct_type_ids alphabetically for deterministic type-id assignment. Good. But the EXISTING struct registration at lines 17357-17369 iterates `keys(e.ire_struct_types)` which is dict insertion order. NOVA dicts are insertion-ordered (line 988: 'dense entries in insertion order'). The insertion order is determined by which make_struct codegen site is visited first (line 15096: `e.ire_struct_types[value] = ...`). If struct types are first encountered in different orders across gen5 vs gen6 (e.g., dead-code elimination in gen5 removes a struct that gen6 keeps, or vice versa), the type-id assignment would differ. The design says 'sort alphabetically' which addresses this, but the EXISTING registration block (lines 17357-17369) that the design KEEPS ('legacy name registration for backward compat') still iterates in insertion order. If the legacy registration emits LLVM IR registers like %sreg.p0, %sreg.p1 etc. keyed by iteration order, and that order differs between gen5/gen6, the .ll files diverge. The design replaces the iteration with sorted order but must also ensure the register numbering scheme produces identical output.
issues.fix: The design must explicitly state that the sreg_i counter at line 17359 iterates over the SORTED list, not keys(e.ire_struct_types). The existing code iterates unsorted keys -- this was already a latent reconverge risk BEFORE this design. Verify whether the current code already produces non-deterministic .ll output (if it does, this is a pre-existing bug that the design should fix, not inherit).

issues.title: json_stringify_value struct case: field values accessed via slots[i+1] without RC inc -- potential use-after-free during recursive serialization
issues.detail: In Section 4A, json_stringify_value recurses into `json_stringify_value(b, slots[i + 1], depth + 1)`. This reads a slot value and passes it to recursive serialization. If a concurrent arena_exit or RC-free fires during serialization (e.g., from another green task that drops the struct), the slot values become dangling pointers. The existing JSON paths (list, dict) have the same pattern, so this is not a NEW vulnerability per se, but the design introduces a longer-lived traversal (struct fields can be deeply nested), increasing the window. More critically: if `nova_rt_elem_to_str` is called on a struct field that is itself a struct, and that inner struct is arena-allocated and the arena is freed mid-serialization, the read of inner struct's slots is a UAF. This is mitigated by NOVA's single-threaded-per-arena model (arenas are per-task, tasks are cooperative), but the mitigation is not stated in the design.
issues.fix: Document the concurrency safety model: serialization runs within a single green task, arenas are per-task and only freed by arena_exit which is called from the same task. If cross-task serialization is ever added, the struct metadata walk would need RC protection.

issues.title: from_json reconstructor uses meta->field_names[i] as a dict key -- string identity mismatch with parsed JSON dict keys
issues.detail: Section 4F's nova_rt_struct_from_json_by_id does `int64_t key = (int64_t)(uintptr_t)meta->field_names[i]; int64_t val = nova_rt_dict_get(dict_val, key);`. This casts the metadata's field name pointer (an interned string in program image) to an i64 and passes it to dict_get. But dict_get (line 2054) casts the key to `const char*` and does `strcmp`. The dict's ACTUAL keys are heap-allocated strings from json_parse (NOVA_MEM_RAW tagged heap strings). The strcmp comparison works correctly because both sides are valid C strings. HOWEVER, the `nova_dict_hash_key` hash function must also produce the same hash for the metadata string and the dict key string. Since both are valid null-terminated C strings hashed by content (DJB2 over chars), this is fine. BUT: the design does not RC-inc the extracted value before storing it in the new struct (`s[i + 1] = val; nova_rc_inc(val)`). If the dict is freed before the struct is used, the struct holds dangling pointers. Actually, looking more carefully, the code DOES call nova_rc_inc(val) after the store. But the dict itself might still be alive (caller holds a ref). The real issue: if a field name in the metadata does NOT exist in the JSON dict, dict_get returns 0, and the struct gets 0 in that slot. For string-typed fields, 0 is a null pointer that will crash on any string operation. The design has no 'missing field' handling.
issues.fix: Add missing-field handling: if dict_get returns 0 for a field, either set a sentinel or return an error. Document that round-trip JSON <-> struct requires all fields present.

issues.title: Metadata globals (@nova_meta_fnames_N) emitted INSIDE @main body or BEFORE it -- design is ambiguous and the wrong choice causes LLVM verifier failure
issues.detail: Section 3C says 'The global arrays (@nova_meta_fnames_N, @nova_meta_ftypes_N) are emitted in the module header section (before all function definitions), not inside @main.' But the design's pseudocode interleaves them within the @main registration loop. LLVM requires global definitions to be at module scope, not inside a function body. The design acknowledges this but the implementation recipe is confusing: it says 'Phase 1: emit field-name and field-type global arrays (before @main body)' but then immediately continues with 'Phase 2: in @main, register each struct's metadata' in the same loop. The compiler currently emits string constants AFTER all functions (line 17412-17416: 'Emit string constants' happens after @main closes). If the metadata globals are emitted in the same section, they appear after @main but are referenced inside @main -- this is legal in LLVM IR (forward references to globals work), but the emission ORDER matters for reconverge: if the globals are emitted in a different section than string constants, the .ll layout changes, which does not break correctness but could cause spurious reconverge failures during development.
issues.fix: Emit metadata globals in the same section as string constants (after @main), using the existing ire_strs accumulator pattern. Use forward references inside @main. This matches the existing pattern and minimizes reconverge risk.

issues.title: Const-baked struct globals are built BEFORE metadata registration -- design acknowledges this but proposes moving registration earlier, which has its own risks
issues.detail: Section 5F acknowledges that const-baked structs (built in @main around line 17064-17078) are created BEFORE the metadata registration block (line 17357). The design proposes 'move the metadata registration block to BEFORE global const initialization.' But const-baking happens inside nova_main (the user-level main), while struct name registration currently happens in @main (the C-level main) BEFORE nova_rt_main_dispatch. Moving metadata registration before const-baking means it must happen before line 17064 in the emission order. This is feasible since both are in @main, but const-baked lists call nova_rt_list_create/nova_rt_list_append -- if those somehow interact with struct metadata (they don't currently), the ordering change could be an issue. The REAL risk: const-baked structs don't exist today (const-baking only handles list aggregates per ir_const_bakeable at line 7068), so this is a non-issue for now. But if const-baked structs are added later, the ordering must be maintained.
issues.fix: The reordering is safe today because no const is a struct. Add a comment noting the ordering invariant so future const-struct-baking respects it.

issues.title: NOVA_STRUCT_NSLOTS macro change silently breaks ALL existing compiled binaries -- no ABI versioning
issues.detail: The existing NOVA_STRUCT_NSLOTS macro is `((ptr[-1] & 0xFFFF) >> 3)` which extracts 13 bits. The new macro is `((ptr[-1] >> 3) & 0x1F)` which extracts 5 bits. Any pre-built NOVA binary (compiled with the old runtime) that links against the new runtime (or vice versa) would misinterpret nslots. For example, a struct with 8 fields (nslots=9, binary 1001) under the old encoding has tag bits 3-15 = 1001 (bits 3-6), which the new NSLOTS macro reads as `(1001 >> 3) & 0x1F` ... wait, the tag is already shifted by 3 in both encodings. The old packed value for 9 slots is `(9 << 3) | 5 = 77` (binary 01001 101). Old NSLOTS: `(77 & 0xFFFF) >> 3 = 9`. New NSLOTS: `(77 >> 3) & 0x1F = 9 & 0x1F = 9`. OK, for values <= 31 both macros agree. For values > 31 the old encoding puts bits in 8-15 which the new macro interprets as type-id. A struct with 40 slots: old packed = `(40 << 3) | 5 = 325` (binary 101000101). Old NSLOTS: `325 >> 3 = 40`. New NSLOTS: `(325 >> 3) & 0x1F = 40 & 31 = 8` -- WRONG. New TYPEID: `(325 >> 8) & 0xFF = 1` -- bogus type-id pointing to some other struct's metadata. This is only an issue for pre-existing binaries with >31-field structs, which the design says don't exist. But if ANY exist in test artifacts or caches, they would silently misinterpret. The ABI stamp mechanism mentioned in the project history should be bumped.
issues.fix: Bump the ABI stamp when this lands. Document that all pre-built binaries must be recompiled.

issues.title: Performance: nova_struct_meta_for does a slot-0 read + comparison on EVERY json_stringify/str/type_name call for structs
issues.detail: nova_struct_meta_for reads NOVA_STRUCT_TYPEID (one shift+mask on tag word), then indexes into g_struct_meta (array index, L1-hot), then reads slot-0 and compares against meta->type_hash (one 8-byte comparison). This is ~5-10ns total, called once per struct during serialization. Serialization is already I/O-bound (string building). GATE 4/5 benchmarks (sieve/primes/matmul) do NOT use json_stringify or str() on structs, so they are completely unaffected. The allocation-time cost is one extra OR and shift -- sub-nanosecond. This is within tolerance. The only hot-path concern is if nova_rt_eq or nova_rt_hash ever calls nova_struct_meta_for for the >31-field fallback, but that is deferred. VERDICT: no GATE 4/5 regression.
issues.fix: No action needed. The cross-check in nova_struct_meta_for could be removed in a future optimization pass if profiling shows it matters.

issues.title: Closure type-id collision: a closure with a trampoline pointer in slot-0 that numerically equals a registered type_hash would pass nova_struct_meta_for's cross-check
issues.detail: Closures use NOVA_MEM_STRUCT tag and store a function pointer in slot-0. If a closure is accidentally allocated with a nonzero type-id (e.g., due to the gen3 bootstrap garbage-argument issue in finding #4), AND the function pointer in slot-0 happens to numerically equal a registered struct's type_hash, nova_struct_meta_for would return that struct's metadata for the closure. Then json_stringify_value would try to render the closure as a struct with named fields, reading capture slots as if they were struct fields -- producing garbage JSON or crashing if a capture value is misinterpreted. The probability is 1/2^64 per closure per registered struct, so effectively zero for a single program run. But: if the gen3 garbage-argument issue (finding #4) causes ALL gen3-emitted closures to get a small nonzero type-id (e.g., the alignment value from aligned_struct_alloc leaking into the register), the cross-check would fail correctly (slot-0 function pointer != registered hash). Still, the design should explicitly ensure closures get type_id=0 rather than relying on probabilistic safety.
issues.fix: Ensure all non-struct allocations (closures, Results, deep_copy) pass type_id=0. The cross-check is a belt-and-suspenders defense, not the primary guard.

verdict: NOT SOUND AS WRITTEN -- requires revision before implementation. The design has 4 fatal issues that would each independently cause a hard revert: (1) deep_copy loses type-id on channel-sent/copy'd structs, (2) nova_result_pack C-level call has wrong arity and would fail to compile, (3) aligned_struct_alloc's internal delegation has wrong arity, (4) gen3 bootstrap codegen emits 1-arg calls to a 2-arg function causing silent memory corruption during bootstrap. All 4 are in the 'missed struct-creation site' category -- the exact failure mode the design's Section 8.4 claims to avoid. The design correctly identifies that nova_rt_struct_alloc is the ONE allocation point, but then only updates the LLVM-emitted call sites in make_struct (line 15087) and forgets the C-level callers (deep_copy, nova_result_pack, aligned_struct_alloc delegation) and the gen3 bootstrap codegen path (line 3987). The nslots 13-bit -> 5-bit reduction is the biggest architectural risk: it introduces a silent correctness cliff at 32 fields that the design acknowledges but defers fixing for eq/hash/deep_copy/rc_free. The compile-time guard mitigates this IF it ships and stays, but the design should ship the metadata fallback for rc_free and deep_copy in S1, not defer to S5 -- a struct leak or under-free is worse than a wrong equality check. The reconverge analysis is mostly sound but the existing unsorted dict iteration (line 17360) is a pre-existing latent bug that should be fixed in the same commit. Biggest risk overall: the 4 missed C-level call sites. These are easy to fix but their omission suggests the design was reasoned about at the LLVM-emission level only, not at the full-system level.
